witnesses.title: Tiny NDJSON presence, heterogeneous-value and malformed-record contract check
witnesses.input: Construct a four-record NDJSON file: {"id":1,"v":null,"label":"東京"}; {"id":2,"label":"naïve"}; {"id":3,"v":7,"label":"Δ"}; {"id":4,"v":"7","label":"x"}; add one malformed fifth line. Use a separately declared schema/adapter policy.
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: DuckDB JSON loading documentation says missing keys become SQL NULL and has explicit auto-detection/sample settings [S3]. Product contract requires either preserving field presence separately or explicitly canonicalizing missing and null. Malformed-record behavior must be checked against the pinned reader and adapter; CSV reject behavior cannot be assumed for NDJSON [S2].
witnesses.expected_result: No silent deletion. A typed table must preserve a presence flag/raw record if null-versus-missing distinction is required; otherwise the UI states both canonicalize to SQL NULL. Integer/string conversion is explicit and error/reject behavior is recorded. Unicode labels round-trip under declared encoding.
witnesses.scope_limits: No engine version, code, stdout/stderr or result is claimed. Exact explicit-JSON-null conversion and malformed-line ledger behavior remain implementation checks.

witnesses.title: Floating reduction order and ordered-versus-unordered result fingerprint check
witnesses.input: Compare float64 left-fold inputs [1e16, 1.0, -1e16] and [1e16, -1e16, 1.0]; also compare the same two-row relation emitted in opposite orders, with duplicate-row and null/type-tag cases added before defining a production canonical encoding.
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: DuckDB documents floating sum as order-sensitive and warns that operators including GROUP BY and joins may not preserve row order [S4, S5]. The two possible floating results in the desk derivation are not an execution receipt. A rolling digest over row encodings is order-sensitive by construction unless rows are canonicalized first.
witnesses.expected_result: Record engine/type/results; never assert floating sum order independence. Treat sequence digest and order-free multiset comparison as separate modes; preserve duplicates in the latter. Hash equality is a compact fingerprint, not a mathematical proof of equality.
witnesses.scope_limits: No code or hashing operation was executed in V01. Exact observed engine results and canonical encoding remain unverified.

witnesses.title: Notebook output association and invalidation against a real kernel
witnesses.input: Create a notebook with source, transform and result cells; deliberately execute cells out of display order; save; restart; edit upstream code; change a registered data hash and environment lock; then fail/cancel a run and remove/corrupt the sidecar.
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: nbformat stores display-order cells, outputs and nullable execution_count but no event/freshness property [S1]. marimo’s DAG precedent documents that static analysis does not track mutation [S6].
witnesses.expected_result: Sidecar event sequence and stable cell ID associate outputs with actual runs. Known changes produce stale; errors produce failed; restart/interruption/missing provenance produce unverified. Unknown dynamic dependencies never remain current by default.
witnesses.scope_limits: No actual notebook client/kernel was available to this read-and-reason V01 workflow.
